title: Find Proteins of Unknown Function (PUFs) using Plantannot - Protocol B
author: Marcos Viana
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgdgjs3w

steps.title: Open Plantannot results page
steps.instruction: Navigate to the Plantannot results page with empty filters using the URL https://www.machado.cnptia.embrapa.br/plantannot/find/?q= or open the Plantannot home page and click the magnifying‑glass icon with the search box empty.

steps.title: Apply organism filter
steps.instruction: In the left‑hand "Organisms" filter, expand the organism list by clicking the green arrow, then select any organism (or leave all boxes empty). For the example, select Oropetium tomaeum, and click "apply".

substeps.instruction: Expand organism list using the green arrow.

steps.title: Apply feature type filter
steps.instruction: In the "Feature type" filter, choose "polypeptide" and click "apply".

steps.title: Apply analyses filters
steps.instruction: In the "Analyses" filter, select both "no diamond matches" and "interproscan matches", then click "apply".

steps.title: Leave other filters empty
steps.instruction: Do not select any options in the "Orthology", "Coexpression", and "Orthologs_coexpression" filters; leave them empty.

steps.title: Search for unknown function
steps.instruction: Enter the text "Unknown function" in the search box at the top of the page and click the magnifying‑glass icon to apply the search.

substeps.instruction: Type "Unknown function" into the search box.

steps.title: View results list
steps.instruction: Observe the "Results" card on the centre‑right of the screen; the filtered list will show Oropetium's proteins of unknown function (8 PUFs were obtained).
